<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

With `--mm-enable-dp-encoder`, each rank keeps a full copy of the MiMo vision tower's weights. But `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` still passed every image and video to `self.visual` on every rank, so each GPU encoded the full multimodal input and the extra ranks added no speedup. This PR spreads MiMo-VL vision encoding across the attention-TP ranks, the way Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and GLM already do. That way, a request with many images or a long video isn't encoded in full on every GPU.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/mimo_v2.py`
  - `get_image_feature` and `get_video_feature` now share one `_encode_visual` path.
  - Without DP encoding, behavior is unchanged: patches are concatenated and encoded with the original `grid_thw`.
  - With DP encoding, inputs go through `run_dp_sharded_mrope_vision_model` with `rope_type="rope_3d"`:
    - Videos are split into single frames (`[t, h, w]` becomes `t × [1, h, w]`) so frames can be balanced across ranks, as `glm5_next` already does. The output is identical because MiMo's vision tower computes its rotary positions, window-attention ordering and `cu_seqlens` per frame.
    - Each rank gets its pixel data through `load_local_pixel_values`, so it only concatenates and encodes the rows it was assigned.
  - Replaced the `assert`s with a check that each item's patch count matches its grid. A mismatch now raises a clear `RuntimeError`.
- `python/sglang/srt/models/mimo_vl.py`
  - Added `MiMoVisionTransformer.out_hidden_size`. The DP helper reads it to build an empty output on a rank that gets no inputs.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_mimo_v2_vision_dp.py` (new, CPU CI `base-a-test-cpu`), which checks that:
  - the non-DP path keeps the packed video grid;
  - the DP path splits a video into frames and the loader returns only the requested rows, for both images and videos;
  - with one rank, the real helper encodes all frames in a single call;
  - with two ranks, a rank that gets no inputs doesn't run the encoder, and receives an output of the right shape (built from `out_hidden_size`) from the owning rank;
  - a patch-count / grid mismatch raises.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: MiMo-V2.6-Pro, TP=EP=8 on 8× H20, `--mm-enable-dp-encoder` on in both runs. Requests went through the OpenAI-compatible chat API, greedy (`temperature=0`), thinking disabled. Inputs are synthetic but generated from fixed seeds, so both runs got identical inputs with known answers:

- **Single image (10):** read a 4-digit number from a 1280×720 image.
- **Multi-image order (6):** 8 images, each showing one character; list them in image order. This checks that per-image embeddings come back in the right order after sharding.
- **Video order (3):** a 48-frame clip showing 6 digits in sequence; list them in order. This checks frame order after the per-frame split. Adjacent repeated digits count as one, because they render as a single longer segment.

| Task | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Single image | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| Multi-image order | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| Video order | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **Total** | **19/19** | **19/19** |

All 19 greedy answers are identical between the two runs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same server and setup as above. Each number is the latency of one chat request with `max_tokens=1`, so it is almost entirely prefill including vision encoding: median of 5 runs after 1 warmup. Every request uses distinct images, so the multimodal embedding cache is never hit. The latency includes about 0.3 s of gateway overhead, shown by the text-only row.

| Workload | Prompt tokens | main | This PR | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Text only | 14 | 0.316 s | 0.336 s | – |
| 1 image, 1280×720 | 896 | 0.691 s | 0.698 s | 0.99× |
| 8 images, 1280×720 | 7,070 | 2.253 s | 1.888 s | **1.19×** |
| 16 images, 1280×720 | 14,126 | 4.073 s | 3.407 s | **1.20×** |
| 64-frame video, 1280×720 | 14,208 | 4.260 s | 3.627 s | **1.17×** |
| 8 concurrent single-image requests (total time) | 896 each | 2.389 s | 2.039 s | **1.17×** |

Multi-image, video and concurrent image requests get 17–20% faster end to end. This saves about 0.37 s at 8 images and about 0.65 s at 16 images or 64 frames. The encoder-only saving is larger than these ratios suggest, because the times also include language-model prefill over about 14k tokens. A single image is unchanged, as expected: one image goes to a single rank either way.

- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+    def _iter_visual_rows(self, items, grid_attr: str):
+        """Yield one packed patch tensor per grid row, in row order."""
+        for item in items:
+            feature = item.feature
+            grids = getattr(item, grid_attr)
+            if feature.dim() != 2 or grids.dim() != 2:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"{grid_attr} feature {tuple(feature.shape)} grid {tuple(grids.shape)}"
+                )
+            counts = [int(n) for n in torch.prod(grids, dim=-1).tolist()]
+            if sum(counts) != feature.shape[0]:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"{grid_attr} rows {feature.shape[0]} != grid patches {sum(counts)}"
+                )
+            start = 0
+            for n in counts:
+                yield feature[start : start + n]
+                start += n
+
+    def _encode_visual(self, items, grid_attr: str) -> torch.Tensor:
+        grids = torch.cat([getattr(item, grid_attr) for item in items], dim=0)
+        rows = list(self._iter_visual_rows(items, grid_attr))
+
+        if not self.visual.use_data_parallel:
+            pixel_values = torch.cat(rows, dim=0).to(dtype=self.visual.dtype)
+            return self.visual(pixel_values, grid_thw=grids)
+
+        if grid_attr == "video_grid_thw":
+            flat_grids = []
+            flat_rows = []
+            for grid, pixels in zip(grids.tolist(), rows):
+                t, h, w = (int(v) for v in grid)
+                frame = h * w
+                for i in range(t):
+                    flat_grids.append([1, h, w])
+                    flat_rows.append(pixels[i * frame : (i + 1) * frame])
+            grids_list = flat_grids
+            rows = flat_rows
+        else:

+"""MiMo's DP vision encoder must not encode a whole clip on every rank."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+import sglang.srt.models.mimo_v2 as mimo_v2
+from sglang.srt.models.mimo_v2 import MiMoV2ForCausalLM
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class _PackedVisual:
+    def __init__(self, use_data_parallel=False):
+        self.use_data_parallel = use_data_parallel
+        self.dtype = torch.float32
+        self.device = torch.device("cpu")
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def __call__(self, pixel_values, grid_thw):
+        self.calls.append((pixel_values.clone(), grid_thw.clone()))
+        return pixel_values
+
+
+class _RecordingGroup:
+    def __init__(self, world_size):
+        self.world_size = world_size
+        self.broadcasts = []
+
+    def broadcast(self, tensor, src):
+        self.broadcasts.append((tuple(tensor.shape), src))
+
+
+def _model(visual):
+    model = MiMoV2ForCausalLM.__new__(MiMoV2ForCausalLM)
+    model.visual = visual
+    return model
+
+
+def _item(feature, **grids):
+    return SimpleNamespace(feature=feature, **grids)
+
+
+def _patch_dp_run(fake_run):
+    return mock.patch.object(mimo_v2, "run_dp_sharded_mrope_vision_model", fake_run)
+
+
+class TestMiMoVisionDpSharding(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_non_dp_keeps_the_packed_video_grid(self):
+        visual = _PackedVisual()
+        feature = torch.arange(12, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(6, 2)
+        item = _item(feature, video_grid_thw=torch.tensor([[2, 1, 3]]))
+
+        out = _model(visual).get_video_feature([item])
+
+        self.assertEqual(len(visual.calls), 1)
+        pixels, grid = visual.calls[0]
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(pixels, feature))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(grid, torch.tensor([[2, 1, 3]])))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, feature))
+
+    def test_dp_splits_a_video_into_frames_and_loads_only_those_rows(self):
+        visual = SimpleNamespace(
+            use_data_parallel=True,
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            device=torch.device("cpu"),
+        )
+        frame0 = torch.full((4, 3), 1.0)
+        frame1 = torch.full((4, 3), 2.0)
+        item = _item(
+            torch.cat([frame0, frame1], dim=0),
+            video_grid_thw=torch.tensor([[2, 2, 2]]),
+        )
+        captured = {}
+
+        def fake_run(vision_model, pixel_values, grid_thw_list, **kwargs):
+            captured["vision_model"] = vision_model
+            captured["pixel_values"] = pixel_values
+            captured["grids"] = grid_thw_list
+            captured["loader"] = kwargs["load_local_pixel_values"]
+            captured["device"] = kwargs["pixel_values_device"]
+            captured["dtype"] = kwargs["pixel_values_dtype"]
+            return torch.zeros(8, 4)
+
+        with _patch_dp_run(fake_run):
+            out = _model(visual).get_video_feature([item])
+
+        self.assertIs(captured["vision_model"], visual)
+        self.assertIsNone(captured["pixel_values"])
+        self.assertEqual(captured["grids"], [[1, 2, 2], [1, 2, 2]])
+        self.assertEqual(captured["device"], visual.device)
+        self.assertEqual(captured["dtype"], visual.dtype)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(captured["loader"]([0]), frame0))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(captured["loader"]([1]), frame1))
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(
+                captured["loader"]([1, 0]),
+                torch.cat([frame1, frame0], dim=0),
+            )
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(out.shape), (8, 4))
+
+    def test_dp_image_loader_returns_the_requested_image_only(self):
+        visual = SimpleNamespace(
+            use_data_parallel=True,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device=torch.device("cpu"),
+        )
+        image0 = torch.arange(6, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(3, 2)
+        image1 = torch.arange(4, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(2, 2) + 10
+        items = [
+            _item(image0, image_grid_thw=torch.tensor([[1, 1, 3]])),
+            _item(image1, image_grid_thw=torch.tensor([[1, 1, 2]])),
+        ]
+        captured = {}
+
+        def fake_run(vision_model, pixel_values, grid_thw_list, **kwargs):
+            captured["grids"] = grid_thw_list
+            captured["loader"] = kwargs["load_local_pixel_values"]
+            return torch.zeros(1, 1)
+
+        with _patch_dp_run(fake_run):
+            _model(visual).get_image_feature(items)
+
+        self.assertEqual(captured["grids"], [[1, 1, 3], [1, 1, 2]])
+        loaded = captured["loader"]([1])
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(loaded, image1.to(torch.bfloat16)))
+        self.assertEqual(loaded.dtype, torch.bfloat16)
+
+    def test_dp_single_rank_encodes_every_frame_in_one_call(self):
+        visual = _PackedVisual(use_data_parallel=True)
+        feature = torch.arange(12, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(6, 2)
+        item = _item(feature, video_grid_thw=torch.tensor([[2, 1, 3]]))
+
+        with get_parallel().override(attn_tp_size=1):
+            out = _model(visual).get_video_feature([item])
+
+        self.assertEqual(len(visual.calls), 1)
+        pixels, grid = visual.calls[0]
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(pixels, feature))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(grid, torch.tensor([[1, 1, 3], [1, 1, 3]])))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, feature))
+
+    def test_dp_rank_without_work_receives_the_owner_output(self):
+        # Not callable: a rank that owns no image must not run the encoder.
+        visual = SimpleNamespace(
+            use_data_parallel=True,
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            device=torch.device("cpu"),
+            spatial_merge_size=2,
+            out_hidden_size=5,
+        )
+        item = _item(torch.zeros(4, 3), image_grid_thw=torch.tensor([[1, 2, 2]]))
+        group = _RecordingGroup(world_size=2)
+
+        with get_parallel().override(
+            attn_tp_size=2, attn_tp_rank=1, attn_tp_group=group
+        ):
+            out = _model(visual).get_image_feature([item])
+
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(out.shape), (1, 5))
+        self.assertEqual(out.dtype, torch.float32)
+        self.assertEqual(group.broadcasts, [((1, 5), 0)])
+
+    def test_patch_count_must_match_the_grid(self):
+        visual = _PackedVisual()
+        item = _item(
+            torch.zeros(3, 2),
+            image_grid_thw=torch.tensor([[1, 2, 2]]),
+        )
+
+        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+            _model(visual).get_image_feature([item])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
